summary: Slate Creek (Lead Hill) L-4 lookout, built 1931 and removed in the 1950s; WillhiteWeb photos show a lookout footing on the summit.

facts.design: L-4 cab (FFLOS calls it an L-4 tower)
facts.status_note: Removed in the 1950s per FFLOS and WillhiteWeb; firelookout.com says destroyed. A lookout footing is shown on the summit in WillhiteWeb photos.

staffing.status: one lookout named (Wayne Myers, 1932); no later staffing found in the sources read

access.note: Walk-in access: the road is gated at the highway April 1 to June 30, and a locked gate sits about 7 miles up. No closure order found in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb lists 2.5 miles one way and 1,100 feet of gain, mostly easy road walking past the locked gate.

events.note: L-4 design; FFLOS calls it a tower, WillhiteWeb calls it a cab
Wayne Myers named as the lookout person, per a 1932 Metaline Falls News item
Sources give only 'the 1950s'; 1950 is a placeholder for that decade. firelookout.com says destroyed

evidence.supports: built in 1931 as an L-4 tower; removed in the 1950s
evidence.quote: Built in 1931, this L-4 tower was removed in the 1950s.

evidence.supports: about 11 miles northeast of Metaline Falls
firelookout.com gives L-4 tower, destroyed in the 1950s
built in 1931 as an L-4 cab; the cab was removed in the 1950s
evidence.quote: In 1931, an L-4 cab was built. The cab was removed in the 1950s.
In 1932, the lookout person was Wayne Myers.

evidence.supports: Metaline Falls News described Myers as stationed above the Leadhill camp
evidence.quote: The Metaline Falls News in 1932 described Wayne as stationed just above the Leadhill camp on Slate creek.

evidence.supports: 1932 newspaper item: lookout job on the Kaniksu forest, stationed above the Leadhill camp
evidence.quote: who has a lookout job on the Kaniksu forest, being stationed just above the Leadhill camp on Slate creek.
Lead Hill summit with lookout footing placed next to the tree.
Currently in 2024, there are superb views due to recent clearcuts along the route.

evidence.quote: Be aware the road is gated at the highway from April 1 to June 30.

evidence.supports: drive 7 miles from July, then a locked gate
evidence.quote: Starting in July, you can drive 7 miles up the road but then there is a permanent looking locked gate.

evidence.supports: easy road walking beyond the gate

Take the signed Slate Creek Road to the right.

evidence.quote: Drive Highway 31 north of Metaline Falls toward Canada.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS calls it an L-4 tower; WillhiteWeb calls it an L-4 cab. The record keeps cab and the story notes both words.
FFLOS and WillhiteWeb say removed in the 1950s; firelookout.com says destroyed. The story reports removal and notes the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Only one staffing record (1932). The brief's 2012 FFLOS registration date was not re-checked in this run. Gate dates come from a WillhiteWeb page written in 2024; confirm before any trip. The record's kind 'tower' is consistent with FFLOS but WillhiteWeb says cab.
